sections.Science News:
#### A diamond maser amplifies microwaves near the quantum-noise limit at millikelvin temperature

A [peer-reviewed *Nature Communications* article published 16 November](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-026-79021-7) reports the first non-superconducting maser amplifier operated near the quantum-noise limit at millikelvin temperature. The device uses nitrogen impurity spins in diamond and microwave pumping, with four-spin cross-relaxation creating population inversion. At **6.595 GHz** it reaches more than **30 dB** maximum power gain; the measured minimum input-referred noise is **3.05 ± 0.23 quanta**, or about **2.55 quanta above the standard half-quantum limit**, corresponding to a noise temperature of approximately **0.96 K**.

The gain profile can be shifted by more than 10 MHz with a static magnetic field. At 20 dB gain the input and output 1 dB compression points are approximately **−85 dBm** and **−65 dBm**, respectively. The result supplies a non-superconducting route to cryogenic microwave amplification, but the noise, bandwidth and tunability remain behind leading superconducting parametric amplifiers. The authors identify imperfect spin inversion, insertion loss and pump power as practical limitations; this is a laboratory amplifier demonstration, not yet a drop-in quantum-computing readout system.

#### US Supreme Court leaves restoration of terminated research grants in place

On **16 November**, the US Supreme Court declined to hear the federal government's appeal in the University of California research-grant case, leaving the lower-court injunction in force. The dispute concerns competitive grants terminated by the National Science Foundation and other agencies because the research was considered inconsistent with the administration's policies on diversity, equity and inclusion. The [Supreme Court's action](https://www.supremecourt.gov/orders/courtorders/111626zor_cb7d.pdf) contained no opinion or merits ruling.

The lower courts found that the researchers had shown a substantial likelihood that the cancellations constituted unconstitutional viewpoint discrimination, and ordered the affected grants restored while litigation continues. Reports differ on the relevant monetary total because they describe different subsets of the wider grant dispute; the [specific appeal covered roughly $59 million according to Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/world/supreme-court-rejects-trump-appeal-defending-diversity-related-grant-cuts-2026-11-16/), while broader University of California terminations were much larger. The denial preserves the existing injunction but does not finally resolve federal authority over research funding or establish a nationwide rule for all cancelled grants.

#### Cryo-electron tomography resolves a functional pore in the poxvirus core

Ye Hong and colleagues used cryo-electron tomography and subtomogram averaging to determine the vaccinia-virus portal complex at **6.7 Å** resolution and its central pore at **4.4 Å**, in a [peer-reviewed *Nature* paper published 16 November](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11399-2). Structural prediction and experimental density identify the viral proteins E8, E6 and L3 as the main pore components. A narrow, positively charged constriction is formed by conserved lysines in L3; replacing these residues impaired viral gene expression and propagation.

Poxviruses transcribe early messenger RNA inside an intact viral core, so they require a route for molecular exchange with the cytoplasm. The channel's dimensions, charge and mutational sensitivity support a portal function, but the study does not directly visualize RNA passing through the pore. A related [independent structure published in July](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10856-2) likewise identified a conserved hexameric E6/E8/L3 complex and connected it to assembly, early-mRNA release and genome uncoating. The new work strengthens the structural model and identifies a functional constriction; therapeutic targeting remains a proposal rather than a demonstrated antiviral strategy.

#### A scalable plasma immunoassay tracks advanced insoluble tau pathology

A [cross-sectional *JAMA* study published online 16 November](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2856953) reports a high-sensitivity immunoassay for endogenously cleaved microtubule-binding-region tau, using **35 μL of plasma** per sample. The analysis included **728 participants**: 521 brain donors from two autopsy cohorts and 207 participants from two tau-PET cohorts. In the autopsy cohorts, adjusted geometric-mean eMTBR-tau concentrations were **25.2-fold and 50.5-fold higher** at Braak stage VI than at stages I–II.

In one imaging cohort, levels were **11.0-fold higher** at tau-PET stages III–IV and **59.9-fold higher** at stages V–VI than at stage 0. Immunoassay measurements correlated strongly with mass-spectrometry eMTBR-tau243 measurements (**Spearman ρ = 0.93** across 108 participants), and both approaches discriminated regional tau-PET positivity with AUCs of **0.96–0.99** in the comparison sample.

This provides proof of principle for a more scalable blood measure of advanced neurofibrillary-tangle burden. It is not a prospective clinical diagnostic validation: the cohorts were cross-sectional, many low-stage measurements fell below the quantification limit, autopsy and imaging cohorts differed, and performance across laboratories and representative clinical populations remains unestablished. Relevant assay patents and industry relationships are disclosed in the article.

#### A Neandertal-derived variant is associated with occipital volume and schizophrenia risk

Hugo Zeberg and Svante Pääbo report in a [peer-reviewed *PNAS* article published online 16 November](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2624837123) that a common Neandertal-derived variant near *DAAM1* is associated with altered *DAAM1* expression and an approximately **0.85 cm³ smaller occipital-lobe volume per copy** in present-day humans. Homozygous carriers had an almost **10% lower relative risk of schizophrenia**, while associations with general cognitive ability and educational attainment were small or absent.

The archaic origin is supported by the haplotype's similarity to Neandertal sequence and its population distribution. The anatomical and disease results are association analyses: they do not show that reduced occipital volume protects against schizophrenia, that *DAAM1* alone mediates the association, or that the variant conveys a general cognitive advantage. Independent expert commentary also cautions against interpreting a small present-day imaging association as a reconstruction of Neandertal cognition. **Evidence access:** the indexed abstract and independent expert commentary were reviewed; the complete methods and supplementary analyses were not accessible at the cutoff.

#### Distinct mouse prefrontal circuits separate sensory and affective pain responses

A [peer-reviewed, open-access *Nature Neuroscience* study published 16 November](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41593-026-02498-4) combines longitudinal two-photon imaging, electrophysiology, viral tracing, fibre photometry, optogenetics and chemogenetics in a mouse spared-nerve-injury model. Peripheral nerve injury sensitized several classes of inhibitory neurons in the prelimbic cortex and shifted their responses from predominantly single-modality to polymodal.

Circuit perturbations separated two components of neuropathic pain. PV⁺ inhibitory neurons gating Rbp4⁺ excitatory output were linked primarily to sensory hypersensitivity, whereas Prox1⁺ inhibitory neurons interacting with Cux2⁺ and Ntsr1⁺ excitatory populations influenced avoidance and affective behaviour through different projections. Several intervention groups contained only **6–9 mice**, although the study used converging anatomical, physiological and behavioural assays. The work maps causal circuitry in this mouse model; it does not establish an equivalent circuit organization in humans or demonstrate a treatment for chronic pain.

#### An aromatic cyclopentadienide ring is embedded in a bowl-shaped nanocarbon

A [peer-reviewed *Nature Chemistry* paper published 16 November](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41557-026-02293-5) reports pentabenzocorannulenide, a curved conjugated carbon framework containing an anionic aromatic cyclopentadienide ring. The five-membered ring forms quantitatively through aromatization-driven nucleophilic dealkylation of a pentabenzocorannulene precursor. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction and quantum-chemical calculations show a bonding and electronic structure distinct from corannulene, fullerenes and carbon-nanotube end caps.

The anion undergoes reversible covalent functionalization and η⁵ metal coordination, demonstrating that an aromatic cyclopentadienide motif can retain useful reactivity when incorporated into a non-planar sp²-carbon network. This is a fundamental synthesis and structure result. Possible applications in molecular electronics, catalysis or functional materials were not demonstrated. **Evidence access:** the publisher abstract and indexed structural conclusions were reviewed; complete experimental yields, spectra and computational sensitivity analyses were not accessible.
